extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 Template from User Input — Remote code execution on the application server, full server compromise [verified: The `name` query parameter flows directly into `Template(content).render()` as template source code (no sanitization, no Jinja2 sandbox), and the Coraza WAF is disabled (`SecRuleEngine Off` in caddy/Caddyfile line 13), so SSTI payloads like `{{config.__class__.__init__.__globals__}}` execute unblocked for RCE.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unescaped name Parameter in HTML Response — Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser context, enabling session hijacking, credential theft, or page defacement [verified: The `name` parameter is f-string interpolated into HTML and rendered via `Template(content).render()` with no HTML escaping or autoescaping configured; Jinja2 passes non-template literal text through unchanged, so `<script>alert(1)</script>` reflects unescaped to the browser, and the WAF's XSS rule is also disabled by `SecRuleEngine Off`.]

Missing HTTP Timeout on Outbound Request Leading to Resource Exhaustion — An attacker can issue concurrent requests to the root endpoint, causing all worker threads to block on hung outbound HTTP connections. The application becomes unresponsive to legitimate traffic, resulting in a denial of service. Combined with the missing rate limiting, this is trivial to exploit. [verified: requests.get() at main.py:31 has no timeout parameter, no rate limiting exists anywhere, no middleware or WAF (SecRuleEngine Off) mitigates—every GET / request triggers an unbounded blocking outbound call on all exposed proxy ports (80/443/1337).]
